title: Spread and rest in arrays, objects, and function calls
hook: Three dots mean two related things: spread expands iterables into elements or properties; rest collects remaining items into a new array or object. Same syntax, opposite direction.

blocks.text: **Spread** (`...`) in array literals and function calls expands an **iterable** into comma-separated values. In object literals, spread copies **own enumerable properties** from source objects (later keys overwrite). **Rest** in destructuring or function parameters collects remaining elements into array/object. **Rest parameters** replace `arguments` object — real Array with proper rest binding.

entries.plainDefinition: Expand iterable or object properties into surrounding literal or call.
Final function parameter collecting extra arguments as array.
Spread creates one level clone — nested objects shared by reference.
Object with Symbol.iterator — Array, String, Map keys, Set.

blocks.text: Immutable updates in React/Redux: `{ ...state, count: state.count + 1 }`. Function calls to Math.max, Promise.all argument lists, and merging config layers. **Shallow copy trap** is a top production bug — nested mutation leaks. C# has **params array** and collection spread via LINQ Concat — not identical semantics.

blocks.title: Interview trap: spread order
blocks.body: Later spread wins on duplicate keys: { ...a, ...b } — b overwrites a. Order is intentional merge strategy.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Expecting deep merge from object spread. Mutating nested object after shallow clone. Rest not last in parameter list. Spreading non-iterable in array context — TypeError.

blocks.text: React state: spread top level only — use immer for deep drafts. Performance: large array spread allocates — consider push with loop in hot paths. **Object spread** copies enumerable own props — skips prototype chain and symbols unless explicit. Know **structuredClone** limits (no functions, some types).

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Calling spread a deep clone. Cannot explain rest must be last parameter. Unaware nested object shared reference after spread.

interviewTakeaways: Spread expands; rest collects — same ... syntax, opposite direction.
Object/array spread is shallow — nested refs shared.
Merge order: later spread overwrites earlier keys.
60s: Spread in literals and calls. Rest in destructure and params. Shallow only — use structuredClone for deep. C# params and Concat analog.
Follow-up: immutable update nested state field without mutating original.
commonPitfalls: Shallow spread then mutating nested property on original.
Rest parameter before other parameters — invalid.
Strong answer: shallow vs deep, merge order, params vs arguments, structuredClone.

jsTsCorrelations.note: TS models object spread intersection — still shallow at runtime after emit.
